gap: No result ChatGPT got states that Rexing's 4-channel R4 installs as only two units (the windshield main body and a rear camera), with the left and right cameras built onto that main body. So the 'side' views come from lenses at the windshield looking out through the front door glass, not from cameras at the doors. Rexing also says the lenses turn 180° and can face the cabin. The R4's side cameras keep recording after the car is parked only with a separately sold Rexing Type-C Smart Hardwire Kit.
standout_why: Compared against Dashlore (cited), which covers only the Vantrue N5S, says nothing about side cameras and says parking mode needs a hardwire kit sold separately; and mydrivecar.com (rank 4/12), which says side views depend on 'mounting angle' and that cameras 'can be rotated' but never says whether the side lenses sit on the windshield unit or the outside of the car. Car and Driver (cited) would not load for me, so I could not check it. ChatGPT's own answer warned in general terms that 'windshield-mounted side cameras record through glass', but none of the result pages I read gives the maker's statement that ties this to its top pick, the Rexing R4 family.
decides: It confirms the side warning in ChatGPT's answer and corrects its top pick. The Rexing R4 and R4 Pro, plus similar units with all lenses on one body such as the REDTIGER F17 Plus and VP40, give side views taken from the windshield. They suit sideswipes while driving and can be turned to face the cabin for rideshare, but they do not reliably catch low door dings while parked, and parked recording also needs a hardwire kit. A shopper who means 'cameras looking along both doors' needs a system with separately cabled left and right cameras (the Botslab G980H lists separate left and right cameras, but I could not open its page to confirm how they mount). Otherwise they should accept windshield side views and pick on front-camera quality and price.

findings.label: Install layout
findings.source_title: The Rexing R4 Enhanced IR Dash Cam Captures 4-Channels All In Real HD
findings.note: Maker's blog. The R4 records four channels (front, left, right, rear), and the rear camera is the separate unit on a 22 ft cable, so the left and right lenses must be on the windshield main unit.

findings.label: Side camera aim
findings.value: Each side camera turns 180°; "You can even choose to turn one or both side cameras in to face your cabin"
findings.source_title: The Rexing R4 Enhanced IR Dash Cam Captures 4-Channels All In Real HD
findings.note: Maker's words: "Both side cameras can be adjusted 180-degrees". The same lenses serve as either side-window views or cabin views.

findings.label: Side camera night lighting
findings.value: 4 IR LEDs per side camera (8 total)
findings.source_title: The Rexing R4 Enhanced IR Dash Cam Captures 4-Channels All In Real HD
findings.note: "Both the left and right side cameras are enhanced with 4 IR lights each". The manual on Manualslib (p. 4) lists "8 IR Lights".

findings.label: Parking monitor power
findings.value: Requires the Rexing Type-C Smart Hardwire Kit, sold separately
findings.note: Manual p. 18: "To enable the Parking Monitor, you'll need to connect it with a Rexing Type-C Smart Hardwire Kit (sold separately)." On the cigarette-lighter plug (p. 11) the camera powers on with the 12 V socket, so parked side recording depends on the hardwire kit.

findings.label: Side camera location (reviewer)
findings.value: Side cameras "connected to the main body", which sits on the windshield by suction cup
findings.source_title: The Gadgeteer review of the Rexing Radar R4-RD (Celeste Miller, 2026-02-16)
findings.note: Celeste Miller also reports the R4-RD runs from the OBD port, which "has a built-in safety that shuts the camera off if the battery for the car gets too low".

findings.label: What the extra two channels see
findings.value: Two IR cabin cameras covering the front and rear seats; parking mode needs a hardwire kit sold separately
findings.source_title: Best Dash Cams: Every Major Model Ranked by Spec | Dashlore
findings.note: Dashlore (cited by ChatGPT) already states this and says nothing about side cameras, so it is the comparison baseline, not new.

findings.label: Rival coverage of side-camera mounting
findings.value: mydrivecar.com: side views depend on "mounting angle"; "A side camera positioned a few degrees incorrectly can lose useful coverage behind a pillar"
findings.note: I read the first 100,000 of 139,944 characters. That part never says whether side cameras mount inside the windshield or outside the car. Its products are PAPAGO G680, HUPEJOS V8 MAX, KEYROO R4, ICESKY S03, Neideso N300 and IIWEY N5.
